transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2027-06-02 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (VP Eng - MistralBridge), Aisha Rahman (Platform Eng), Tom Baxter (CTO)

Summary: quick partner discovery - MistralBridge is evaluating Redwood for an on-prem/private inference tier to support latency-sensitive SaaS customers. Primary concerns: network constraints, key management, model quantization, cost vs latency. They asked about canary rollouts, KV cache behavior behind NAT, and audit logs.

Topics covered: intro, current stack, deployment constraints, security/compliance, performance expectations, pilot next steps.

[00:00] Marcus Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - Marcus from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick round of intros, then Priya will take us through the runtime capabilities and we'll dig into your infra constraints.
[00:14] Carlos Mendes: Hey Marcus, Carlos here, VP of engineering. We've got Aisha and Tom on. Appreciate the time.
[00:19] Tom Baxter: Hi all.
[00:22] Aisha Rahman: Morning/afternoon.
[00:27] Priya Shah: Thanks. So quick agenda - figure out MistralBridge goals, what "on-prem" means for you, SSO/KMS requirements, perf targets, and a pilot scope.
[00:40] Carlos Mendes: High level - we run a multi-tenant SaaS that needs sub-150ms p95 for short text completions. Some customers require data to never leave our VPC. We're evaluating hybrid - hosted for most customers, private (VPC or on-prem appliance) for sensitive ones.
[00:58] Marcus Lee: Got it. When you say "on-prem appliance" do you mean air-gapped hardware in customer datacenter or colocated racks you manage?
[01:08] Carlos Mendes: We're thinking both—some customers want true on-prem, but others would accept a single-tenant VPC in their region. Flexibility is key.
[01:18] Priya Shah: Redwood Private supports both patterns: customer-managed on-prem plus private control plane with VPC peering. We have an option for on-prem bundles; note: some optimizations like pre-warmed KV caches need an initial sync.
[01:31] Aisha Rahman: Does the KV cache do cross-node sync? Our request patterns are very prefix heavy so caching would make a big difference.
[01:40] Priya Shah: Short answer: cache is local per serving pool, but we offer prefix/KV cache warming and shared cache layers inside a dedicated pool. For strict on-prem single node you'd rely on local KV cache plus Redwood's batching.
[01:54] Tom Baxter: And what about quantized model variants—do you auto-fallback to fp16 vs int8? Our ops team worries about voice-of-customer quality regressions.
[02:05] Priya Shah: We support quantized variants and kernel selection is runtime-driven. We can pin versions for rollouts. For quality-sensitive customers we recommend canary rollouts with evaluation prompt sets.
[02:18] Marcus Lee: On the pricing side we'll discuss dedicated vs private pricing after we scope throughput. But first technical fit. Carlos, can you share current RPS and token distribution?
[02:31] Carlos Mendes: Ballpark 200 rps at peak for short completions, averaging 20 tokens per response. We can provide traces. Important: TCP/UDP egress is tightly controlled.
[02:42] Aisha Rahman: Yep, our egress goes through a NAT gateway and we need allowed IP ranges. If Redwood Private reaches out to arbitrary IPs that's a blocker.
[02:52] Marcus Lee: We can publish fixed egress endpoints and support outbound-only peering. For on-prem we run the runtime inside your VPC so egress is under your control. We'll send firewall/inbound/outbound ports.
[03:05] Priya Shah: Also, for customers who want low latency we recommend colocating model shards on local GPUs and enabling continuous batching tuned to the short sequence length distribution.
[03:18] Tom Baxter: GPU types—do you have validated profiles (A100, H100, L40s)? We run mixed workloads and would like guidance on instance selection.
[03:29] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood's model catalog maps recommended hardware per model. For short completions H100/80GB or L40s with int8 quantization are typical. We'll share our internal perf matrix but we'll want to run a pilot with your dataset.
[03:43] Carlos Mendes: About security—SOC2 is a must. Can you share compliance docs? Also makes a difference whether keys can be customer-managed.
[03:53] Marcus Lee: We have SOC2 and ISO artifacts we can share. For Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM; Redwood integrates with KMS via a connector. We'll attach an architecture note.
[04:05] Aisha Rahman: Do you support HSM-backed keys on-prem? Our financial customers insist on HSM.
[04:12] Priya Shah: On-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS11. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in their cloud account. There are some ops caveats we can outline.
[04:24] Tom Baxter: Does audit log retention live in our account for Private? We need immutable logs for 7 years for certain customers.
[04:33] Marcus Lee: Yes, Private can stream audit logs to your storage. Retention is configurable; we can also push to a SIEM.
[04:40] Carlos Mendes: Nice. I want to understand failure modes—if a node goes down does traffic failover increase latency?
[04:48] Priya Shah: We have smart routing and graceful degradation. If a serving pool is degraded requests route to a fallback model/region. That may impact latency, but avoids hard errors. We recommend an SLA policy per customer class.
[05:01] Aisha Rahman: How are secrets and config sync handled across on-prem and cloud? We have strict change control.
[05:08] Priya Shah: Config is managed via the private control plane; for on-prem case we have a pull model where local agents pull signed configs. We also support RBAC and SAML SSO for operator access.
[05:20] Carlos Mendes: Good. Can you talk a little about deployment automation? We use Ansible/Terraform and would like to templatize install.
[05:28] Marcus Lee: We provide Terraform modules and an Ansible playbook for on-prem installation. For Private we also offer a Helm chart for Kubernetes-managed clusters.
[05:37] Tom Baxter: About networking—we need to avoid opening inbound ports. You said outbound-only peering works?
[05:44] Marcus Lee: Yes, outbound-only is supported for the control plane, and we can leverage VPN peering or private link depending on cloud. We'll include options in the doc.
[05:53] Priya Shah: On performance, for your 200 rps target, do you want line-level p95 of 150ms or end-to-end including network?
[06:02] Carlos Mendes: End-to-end. If we push model to on-prem it should be consistent.
[06:08] Priya Shah: Ok. We'll model that in the benchmark. For example: with L40s and int8 we expect sub-120ms token latency for short seqs under 200 rps with continuous batching and pre-warmed KV. But real numbers need your workload.
[06:25] Marcus Lee: Quick question—any regulatory constraints around residency? EU-only?
[06:29] Carlos Mendes: Some customers in EU and APAC require data to remain in-region. We have a mix.
[06:36] Marcus Lee: We can target regional private deployments; Redwood supports region pinning and routing by policy.
[06:43] Aisha Rahman: On the topic of costs—what's the delta between Dedicated and Private? Rough ranges will help us decide pilot sizing.
[06:51] Marcus Lee: Dedicated is generally lower ops for you but less isolation; Private has higher starting cost due to control plane and infra footprint. We'll provide a pro forma after we size the pilot.
[07:03] Tom Baxter: For the pilot, we want to validate both perf and key rotation with our HSM. Can Redwood do a two-week perf run with our traffic shape?
[07:12] Priya Shah: Yes. We'll propose a 2-week pilot: week 1 smoke/perf runs and week 2 soak tests. We'll need sample traces and access patterns.
[07:22] Carlos Mendes: One more thing—how do you handle model updates and evals to prevent regressions? We can't have silent quality drops.
[07:30] Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to evaluation prompt sets. We can set alerts for regressions and block rollouts if metrics drop beyond thresholds.
[07:40] Marcus Lee: Any blockers on the compliance side that would prevent a pilot?
[07:44] Tom Baxter: Only HSM integration and firewall rules—if those are resolvable we'll proceed.
[07:50] Marcus Lee: We'll send the SOC2 snapshot, HSM integration notes, and a preliminary pilot SOW.
[07:56] Carlos Mendes: Great.
[08:00] --- Technical deep dive (Priya to whiteboard) ---
[08:12] Priya Shah: Walkthrough of runtime: serving pool -> continuous batching -> KV cache -> compiled kernels. In on-prem we use local NVMe for KV persistence and warm the LRU during boot using a provided prefix list.
[08:32] Aisha Rahman: Are we able to control the cache TTLs and eviction?
[08:36] Priya Shah: Yes, eviction TTLs are configurable. For tight memory footprints we can set cache hints per model.
[08:44] Tom Baxter: If we want to run a smaller model variant at peak to save cost, can routing switch automatically?
[08:52] Priya Shah: You can define routing policies by cost/latency/region. Automatic fallback to cheaper model variants is supported, and we can throttle traffic per customer.
[09:03] Carlos Mendes: About observability, can we get token-level traces and latency breakdowns?
[09:08] Marcus Lee: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, model-level traces, and we can stream metrics to Prometheus or Datadog.
[09:16] Aisha Rahman: Will the logs with PII be redacted? We have to comply with privacy regs.
[09:21] Marcus Lee: We support redaction rules and allow logs to be kept in your environment only.
[09:27] Priya Shah: For the performance run we'll want a replay harness—if you have trace files we can replay them deterministically against the runtime.
[09:36] Carlos Mendes: We'll export traces. How do you simulate cold starts for caching?
[09:41] Priya Shah: We'll run both cold and warm scenarios. Cold starts include model load times and cache population; warm runs assume pre-warmed KV cache.
[09:49] Tom Baxter: Any limitations around container runtime or kernel versions for on-prem?
[09:55] Priya Shah: We support a narrow matrix of OSes and container runtimes; we'll send the supported versions list. For on-prem GPU drivers we require specific driver versions for H100/A100.
[10:06] Marcus Lee: I'll add driver/OS requirements in the doc pack.
[10:10] --- Security / compliance Q&A ---
[10:18] Carlos Mendes: Walk me through the KMS/HSM flow end-to-end for on-prem.
[10:23] Priya Shah: Keys can stay in your HSM. The runtime uses envelope encryption - a local key decrypts model artifacts, the local key is sealed to the HSM. For signing and key rotation we call your HSM via PKCS11 over an internal network.
[10:36] Aisha Rahman: Do operators ever see plaintext model keys?
[10:39] Priya Shah: No. Access is via RBAC and KMS operations are audited. We provide audit streams.
[10:46] Tom Baxter: How does rotation work with active sessions?
[10:49] Priya Shah: We use key-rolling with session tokens; active sessions continue with the old key until renewal window. We'll document rotation procedures.
[10:58] Marcus Lee: We'll include a high-level sequence diagram in the pack.
[11:02] Carlos Mendes: Ok thanks.
[11:05] --- Pricing and pilot framing ---
[11:10] Marcus Lee: For pilot we'd propose a time-boxed SOW: infra sizing (2 H100-equivalent nodes or 4 L40s depending on quantization), 2-week run, success criteria: p95 < 150ms, <1% error rate, HSM integration validated.
[11:26] Tom Baxter: Sounds reasonable. Can we include an A/B compare to CloudVendorX? We have a PoC there and want apples-to-apples.
[11:35] Marcus Lee: We can run the same traces against Redwood Private and the CloudVendorX baseline as part of the perf report, subject to non-disclosure constraints.
[11:44] Aisha Rahman: We'll want a cost estimate as well—per-hour TCO for the nodes and license.
[11:50] Marcus Lee: We'll provide that.
[11:53] Priya Shah: On benchmarking we also measure tail behavior; we'll instrument cold start percentiles as well as warm p95.
[11:59] Carlos Mendes: Good.
[12:03] --- Clarifying operational responsibilities ---
[12:10] Aisha Rahman: In a Private model who is on-call for runtime failures?
[12:15] Marcus Lee: For Private we offer optional managed ops (Redwood on-call + on-call handoff) or customer-managed with runbooks. For pilots we usually run jointly to accelerate.
[12:27] Tom Baxter: SLA targets? Our procurement will ask.
[12:31] Marcus Lee: We offer SLA packages for Dedicated and Private; pilot uses best-effort, then we lock SLAs in contract.
[12:38] Carlos Mendes: Ok. Anything else we should know?
[12:42] Priya Shah: One operational note: if you plan to use a lot of single-tenant VPCs we recommend automation for cluster bootstrapping to reduce operator overhead.
[12:53] Carlos Mendes: We'll need Terraform modules for that.
[12:57] Marcus Lee: We'll include the modules and examples.
[13:02] --- Wrap and recap ---
[13:10] Marcus Lee: Quick recap: Redwood will send SOC2 summary, HSM/KMS integration notes, driver/OS matrix, pilot SOW draft and perf plan. Priya will propose benchmark slots. MistralBridge will send sample traces, network topology, and data residency specifics.
[13:28] Tom Baxter: Timeline-wise we want to kick pilot in two weeks if everything lines up.
[13:34] Marcus Lee: We'll aim for that. Any final questions?
[13:39] Aisha Rahman: None from me.
[13:41] Carlos Mendes: Thanks everyone.
[13:43] Marcus Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with the doc pack and proposed dates.
[13:48] --- End of call (meeting lasted ~58 minutes) ---

Notes on transcript quality: some names and product terms auto-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> "K V cache", HSM spelled out inconsistently), occasional filler words and overlaps.
